subject: Post-discovery: cross-region language risk assessment & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>, Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@tokyo-pay.jp>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-discovery: cross-region language risk assessment & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — useful call. Quick recap oriented around the specific language risks you flagged and our suggested next steps so we can scope a small pilot.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Priority locales: EU (IT, FR, DE) and APAC (JA, KO).
- Primary concerns: correctness for finance-specific terms, hallucination on regulatory language, and latency targets for JA/KR flows.
- Data residency & PII handling will be a gating requirement for procurement.

Our immediate recommendations for an evaluation pilot:
1) Two model variants to compare in a 2-week pilot:
   - Variant A: redwood/l10n-small-v2 (optimized for locale prompts; 8k context)
   - Variant B: redwood/large-general-quant-8bit (higher-capacity quantized variant for throughput)
2) Targeted prompt sets: we attached finserv_eval_promptset_v1.csv with 120 locale-specific prompts (IT/FR/DE/JA/KO). Please review and flag any customer-owned phrases to redact.
3) Benchmarks: initial topline summary attached (benchmarks_eu_apac_summary.pdf). We ran small dev runs and saw elevated hallucination rates in JA for currency/IBAN examples versus FR/DE.
4) Mitigations to test in pilot: prefix KV caching for repeated templates, localized few-shot exemplars, and soft-constrained decoding for numeric tokens.

Questions for you to confirm so we can scope pricing and schedule:
- Do you require EU-only hosting for the pilot (data residency)?
- Do you have a PO window or procurement lead we should loop in?
- Any additional locales to include?

Proposed next steps (if you approve):
- We kick off a 2-week canary (instrumented telemetry + eval harness) next Monday.
- Deliver interim results after 5 business days and a short readout at the end.

Attachments: finserv_eval_promptset_v1.csv, benchmarks_eu_apac_summary.pdf

Happy to hop on a short follow-up if helpful — I can coordinate with Neha for the demo.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 01:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: cross-region language risk assessment & next steps

Thanks Grace — useful summary. A few quick answers and clarifications from our side:

- Data residency: yes, for the pilot we need EU-only hosting and encryption-at-rest with customer-managed keys (we can share KMS details after NDA).
- SOC2 / security evidence: please include any SOC2 / ISO27001 artifacts or a summary of compliance posture. Procurement will ask.
- On the prompt set: can you share 5 sample Italian and French prompts rendered through each candidate model (example outputs) so our SMEs can see the error modes? The CSV helps, but we need realistic output samples to evaluate hallucination patterns.

We noted your comment about higher hallucination in JA for numeric tokens — that's a big concern for banking flows. Can you also indicate how you define and measure "hallucination rate" in the attached benchmark summary? Is that model-generated factual mismatch vs ground truth or safety taxonomy hits?

If you can send the sample outputs + SOC2 summary we can triage internally and get a procurement contact to you by end of week.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of AI Programs, FinServ EU
elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com
From: Kenji Saito <kenji.saito@tokyo-pay.jp>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 03:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: cross-region language risk assessment & next steps

Appreciate the recap — two operational questions from our engineering side:

1) Latency & quantization: for JA flows we have a strict target of ~<450ms p95 for 1–2k token responses. Can you provide expected p95 latency numbers for both Variant A (l10n-small-v2) and Variant B (large-general-quant-8bit) on a Dedicated cluster profile, and whether prefix caching reduces that p95 materially?

2) Token cost / budgeting: for budgeting we'd like a quick token-cost estimate assuming 100k tokens/month for each variant (include any delta from CJK tokenization). That will determine which model we pilot first.

If you can include sample outputs for JA from both variants (Kenji) and the token/latency estimates, we can decide which variant to prioritize.

On quoting: Kenji — we can work with your procurement once Elena confirms EU hosting; Kenji-san, for APAC pilot we'll need to confirm data path / routing constraints.

Thanks,
Kenji Saito
Engineering Lead, Tokyo Pay (Prospect)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Aug 2028 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: cross-region language risk assessment & next steps

Internal — plan & owners based on customer asks.

Summary of asks to cover in the pilot package we send to FinServ:
- SOC2/compliance artifacts (security team) — Vivek, can you pull the SOC2 summary + KMS integration note and confirm EU-only deployment options?
- Sample outputs: we need 5 prompt-output pairs for each locale (IT/FR/DE/JA/KO) for both Variant A/B. Marissa, please run the suite against the prompt CSV and capture the raw outputs and basic diffs.
- Hallucination metric: define as any numeric/identifier mismatch to gold (IBAN/account/currency) + free-text factual mismatch flagged by SME. We'll produce a short rubric and tooling to compute hallucination_rate per-locale. Marissa, add this to the eval harness.
- Latency & cost: I will produce a 100k-token cost estimate and expected p95 latency using our Dedicated 2xA100-equivalent profile with/without prefix caching.
- Procurement: Grace, please confirm the primary contact we should send the PO template to (attached pilot_scope_and_po_template.docx).

Deliverables & timeline (internal target):
- Baseline locale eval + sample outputs: 5 business days (Marissa)
- SOC2 + KMS summary: 2 business days (Vivek)
- Pilot quote + cost/latency estimates: 2 business days (Neha)
- Customer readout / decision point: target end of next week once samples + artifacts are in their hands.

I'll assemble a single package (sample outputs, rubric, cost break) into the Drive folder and share the link with Elena & Kenji once ready. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleBenchmarks

Thanks — tagging owners inline.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0124
